title: Adding transaction savepoints interpolated the caller-supplied savepoint name into SAVEPOINT/ROLLBACK TO/RELEASE statements with f-strings.

findings.explanation: This PR fixes a SQL injection vulnerability in savepoint name handling. Previously, user-controlled savepoint names were interpolated directly into SQL strings (e.g., f'SAVEPOINT {name}') without any validation. The fix introduces a strict allowlist validator (validate_savepoint_name) that only permits ASCII letters, digits, hyphens, and underscores. This validator is now called before every SQL string interpolation involving the savepoint name in both postgres.py and sqlite.py. The allowlist is sufficiently restrictive to prevent SQL injection.
This PR does not introduce or modify any authorization logic, endpoint access controls, or object ownership checks. It is purely a defensive input-validation fix for savepoint name injection.
